layouts.name: Doc page (top tabs beside the title)
layouts.api: new Doc({ meta: import.meta, title, subject, methods, properties, notes, files, overview, content(){} }) — Doc extends Page (Doc.js:29); a page opts in by being a Doc instance instead of a plain Page.

tab_alignment.position: beside the title, in the same row as the title well
tab_alignment.css_rule: .page.doc-page { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; } .page.doc-page > .tabs { display: contents; } .page.doc-page > .tabs > .tab-bar { background: var(--well); flex: 1 1 24em; align-items: flex-end; } (Doc.css:11-24, 66-87)

layouts.name: Column pages (page split into side-by-side columns)
layouts.api: this.columns({ even = false, fit = "floor" } = {}) called from a page's initialize() (Page.class.js:803); sets this.columnar = true.

layouts.name: Inner left nav / switcher (vertical tab rail)
defined_in: public/framework/ext/tabs/switcher.js (the actual method — core/ only holds the skin/docs since imports flow down)
layouts.api: import "/framework/ext/tabs/switcher.js"; then this.switcher("guide api reference", { skin: "tree" | "nav" }) — wraps this.tabs(names).ac("vertical").
layouts.page_js_count_grep: rg -l "\.switcher\(" public --glob "page.js" (real non-demo caller: public/framework/ux/Auth/Auth.js, which is not a page.js)

tab_alignment.position: vertical rail down the left side — it IS the nav, not a title-adjacent strip
tab_alignment.css_rule: n/a (no top-tab positioning rule; see switcher.css for the rail layout)

layouts.name: Floating page (persistent left nav beside a capped-width page)
layouts.api: import floating from ".../layout/floating/floating.js"; floating(box, { nav: [{label, href, active}], content: fn }) — a factory function (class Floating), not a Page subclass; box may be null to draw into the current captor.
examples: AI 2 workspace view (ai2/floating.js re-export, per floating.js header comment)

tab_alignment.position: not tabs — a sticky left nav (.floating-nav, position: sticky; top: var(--pad)), collapsing to a top strip under 44em

layouts.name: AI 2 shell (inbox/rail dashboard)
layouts.api: Not a reusable API other pages opt into — it is this one Page's own content(), building .ai2-head (doc-well + tabs) and .ai2 (rail/detail/sub grid) directly; a view joins it only via route() inside page.js.
layouts.page_js_count_grep: grep for ai2-head / "tabs block" across **/page.js — only public/framework/ai2/page.js builds this shell

tab_alignment.position: right-aligned (a bug, not a design choice)
tab_alignment.css_rule: public/framework/ai2/ai2.css:1082-1084 sets .ai2-tab-needs{order:1} .ai2-tab-inbox{order:2} .ai2-tab-overview{order:3} on the three real tabs (added 2026-09-29 for an inbox-lighting trick). public/framework/ext/tabs/tabs.css:133 appends a filler pseudo-element to every .tabs.block bar — .tabs.block > .tab-bar::after { content:""; flex:1; border-bottom:1px solid var(--line); } — with no order of its own, so it defaults to order:0. Flex sorts by order first, so the flex:1 filler (meant only to extend the rule past the last tab) sorts BEFORE the three tabs and eats all the free space, shoving the tabs flush right. Confirmed live: getComputedStyle(bar,'::after').order === "0". No other .tabs.block strip on the site sets per-tab order, so this is the only page affected.

layouts.name: browse() — filter rail + wall of bands
layouts.api: page.browse(bands, tokens, options) — bands = { Label: "child child" }; tokens = CSS custom props (e.g. --column); options = { cap, facets, search, rail }. Called from content().

layouts.name: catalog() — persistent card rail beside a routed child page
layouts.api: initialize(){ this.catalog(); } — no args, called at construction; turns the page's own content() into an "intro" child and rewrites this.content to render the split view.

layouts.name: demo.tree() — a live Page preview card in a wall
layouts.api: new Page(demo.tree({ meta: import.meta, tree: treeFn, rail: true, min: "18em" })) — tree must be a function (never an already-built Page), because Page memoizes .view.
layouts.dom_marker: .page-preview.tree-preview (card; .page-preview-thumb holds the live half-scale box()); the wall grid itself is the shared .page-previews grid defined in Page.class.js
layouts.note: browse(), catalog() and demo.tree() all ultimately draw the same card shape (.page-preview) inside the one shared .page-previews grid — they are different arrangements of one card wall, not three different card shapes.

layouts.name: Site shell / .page.standard (the default page shape)
layouts.api: Automatic — every Page renders div.c("page flow", ...).ac(this.classes ?? "standard") unless the page sets its own classes: (e.g. "full", "topic") to opt out. Sidebar is opt-in per app via new Sidebar({ brand, root: this }), not wired globally in app.js.
layouts.page_js_count: not a meaningful opt-in count — this is the default for every page that does NOT set classes:; 150 page.js files override it with classes: (grep -rl "classes:" public --include=page.js), and the remaining large majority stay .standard by doing nothing

realms.finding: Almost entirely built on the shared layout APIs. The hub pages use plain Page + content() + this.previews() inside /imagine/'s own columns() host. Tab-style children use the real ext/tabs API directly (this.tabs().ac("vertical") or this.tabs("alpha beta gamma delta")). /imagine/cms/doc/page.js is default .page.standard with route(). The one deliberate custom shell is /imagine/scenes/page.js (and its Scene subclass): it sets scenic: true / width: "full" and owns its own 3D build()/tick() render loop, explicitly opting out of the columns host — documented as intentional. /imagine/platform/research/** pages use Program.Topic (ext/Research), a different shared abstraction, not a hand-rolled shell.

Mixed, appropriately, since the realm's subject is layouts itself. public/layouts/page.js and most labs/* pages use plain Page + this.previews()/this.browse() (public/layouts/browse/page.js explicitly notes it used to hand-roll its grid and was migrated onto ext/catalog's browse()). The genuinely custom shell is public/layouts/shell/page.js: it overrides render() itself, builds a drag-resizable rail + viewport via its own Shell.js, and documents the three obligations core/Page imposes on anyone who does this (set this.view, carry .page, never nest a second .page). public/layouts/labs/shells/** pages are also deliberately custom, one Shell instance per whole-app-chrome shape being demonstrated — the lab's explicit purpose, not an oversight.

reimplementations.what: Hand-builds .tabs/.tab-bar/.tab markup and a .tab-panel region itself via a local tabs() helper, plus its own mini Page instances as the demo app.
reimplementations.should_use: this.tabs() (ext/tabs) — the file says so itself: it's hand-wired only because this is a demo-app sandbox with no real Router for tabs() to talk to. Not a bug in place, but a real re-implementation if copied outside a demo context.

reimplementations.what: Wires .tabs .tab-bar .tab markup by hand for a category strip.
reimplementations.should_use: this.tabs() — self-documented as unavoidable here because this.tabs() mutates the page it's called on and this frame renders three times (for twin/thumbnail views), so a deliberate, explained exception rather than a miss.

reimplementations.what: Builds its own .grid.auto card wall with a hand-written demo_card() method, grouped by mechanism, instead of this.previews().
reimplementations.should_use: this.previews() (or a grouped variant of it) — plausible genuine re-implementation, though defensible since it needs mechanism-based grouping that previews() doesn't natively support.
